terms.comment: The diminutive of anas, duck. In Plautus it is also a pet name, “duckie” (Lewis & Short).

terms.grammar: pullus, pullī m., with the genitive of anas
evidence: Cic. N. D. 2.124: anitum ōva … ē quibus pullī ortī
terms.comment: Any young bird is a pullus (see chick). The genitive plural is anatum or the older anitum.

phrases.english: Look, the ducklings are swimming behind their mother!

phrases.latin: serpere anguiculōs, nāre anaticulās, ēvolāre merulās, cornibus ūtī vidēmus bovēs
phrases.english: we see little snakes crawl, ducklings swim, blackbirds fly off, and oxen use their horns

phrases.latin: anitum ōva gallīnīs saepe subpōnimus; ē quibus pullī ortī prīmō aluntur ab hīs ut ā mātribus
phrases.english: we often put ducks’ eggs under hens; the chicks that hatch from them are at first reared by the hens as by their mothers

sources: Lewis & Short: anaticula · Lewis & Short: anas · Lewis & Short: pullus
